resources.string: Help
Answers to common questions. They work without the internet.
Still stuck? Report a problem from Settings: an email you see and can change before it is sent.
How KeepClear works

KeepClear looks at what takes space on this phone and sorts it into three groups.

Clean now: files that are safe to remove, like temporary files, thumbnails and old WhatsApp statuses. One button frees up the space.

Choose what to delete: things only you can decide on, like screenshots, big videos and copies of the same photo. Nothing is deleted until you choose.

Back up: photos and videos worth keeping. KeepClear copies them to a USB drive and checks every copy. Space on the phone comes back only after a second check, and only when you tap "Free up space".
Is it safe?

KeepClear never deletes anything without your tap, and never in the background.

Most of what you clean waits 30 days in the trash, so you can restore it. Files that rebuild themselves are deleted right away.

KeepClear never touches WhatsApp chats and their backups, the drive you back up to, or files you chose to keep.

Right before it deletes anything, KeepClear checks each file again. A file that changed since the scan is left where it is, and you are told.

Nothing leaves the phone except the copies you back up to a place you chose. There are no ads, no tracking and no account.

Test mode: the test version starts in test mode. A line at the top of every screen says so, and nothing is deleted or moved; you only see what would happen.
What is deleted for good, and what goes to the trash

To the trash, for 30 days: duplicates, files you chose to delete, unpacked archives and everything else you clean. You can restore them from the trash. After 30 days KeepClear deletes them for good.

Deleted for good right away: files that rebuild themselves (thumbnails, temporary files, system leftovers, WhatsApp statuses older than a day) and files that were already in another app's bin, like the gallery's bin. There is nothing to restore: the phone makes them again, or they were already deleted once.

After a checked backup: "Free up space" deletes the originals from the phone for good. The copy on the USB drive, checked file by file, is how you restore them. If you prefer, turn on "Keep the original in the 30-day trash too (frees no space)" in Settings.

Emptying the trash deletes what is in it for good. KeepClear asks first.
How to restore a file

From the trash: tap "Trash" at the top of the screen, find the file by its date or name, and tap "Restore". It goes back to where it was. Files stay in the trash for 30 days.

From a backup: connect the USB drive, open the Backup tab and tap "Restore from a backup". Choose whole months or single photos. KeepClear checks each file and restores it to its folder; if that place is taken, it goes to the restore folder instead.

Files deleted for good right away (thumbnails, temporary files) don't need restoring: the phone makes them again.
Why KeepClear asks to see all files

With your permission to see photos and videos, KeepClear finds screenshots, big videos and what to back up.

WhatsApp keeps its photos and videos in its own folder, and old phones and other apps leave folders behind. To see those, KeepClear asks for access to all files. It only reads them on this phone and never sends them anywhere.

KeepClear also works without it: choose WhatsApp's folder once instead, and everything else stays as it is.

You can turn the access off at any time in Android's settings.
Why KeepClear asks for access

With your permission to see photos and videos, KeepClear finds screenshots, big videos and what to back up.

WhatsApp keeps its photos and videos in its own folder. To see it, KeepClear asks you to choose that folder once, in Android's own folder picker. It only reads what is there on this phone and never sends it anywhere.

You can take the access back at any time in Android's settings.
What happens to WhatsApp

KeepClear never touches your chats, their backups or WhatsApp's database.

WhatsApp statuses older than a day are deleted for good: WhatsApp no longer shows them.

Photos, videos and documents you sent or received can be chosen for deleting or backed up, like any other file. Copies of photos you sent, when the same photo is still in your gallery, are offered for cleaning and go to the trash for 30 days.

After you back up WhatsApp media and free up space, the chat shows that the file isn't available. The copy is kept in the backup.
The backup stopped: what to do

Nothing is lost: what was copied and checked stays on the drive, and the backup continues from where it stopped.

The USB drive was unplugged: connect it again and tap "Continue".

The USB drive is full: KeepClear says how much space is needed. Delete what you don't need from the drive, use a bigger one, or choose fewer photos this time.

The battery is low: at 10% the backup pauses by itself, and it continues once the phone is charging.

The phone stopped the backup to save battery: open KeepClear and tap "Continue". Allowing notifications helps the backup keep running.

Anything else: the Backup tab says what happened, with one button to go on. If it keeps happening, report a problem from Settings.
New phone

Install KeepClear on the new phone and connect the USB drive with your backup.

On the first screen tap "New phone? Restore from a backup", or later open the Backup tab and tap "Restore from a backup".

Choose the backup and the months you want. KeepClear checks each file before it writes it and restores it to the folder it was in. If the new phone doesn't have enough free space, KeepClear says so before it starts.

The old phone's trash doesn't move with you: restore what you need from it before you switch.
KeepClear\'s storage and uninstalling

In Android's settings, KeepClear's storage page shows "Manage space" instead of "Clear storage". Clearing KeepClear's data would erase the list of what is in the trash, and the files in it could not be restored. "Manage space" opens a KeepClear screen that shows what the trash holds and opens the trash, where you can empty it.

When you uninstall KeepClear, Android asks whether to keep its data. Keep it if you may install KeepClear again: the trash list and your settings stay. Without it, files left in the trash stay on the phone and KeepClear can't restore them.

Before uninstalling for good, restore what you need from the trash, then empty it.
Private space

Android 15 and later can keep apps in a private space, locked separately from the rest of the phone.

KeepClear can't see the apps and files inside the private space: they are not scanned, cleaned or backed up, and they are not counted in the sizes KeepClear shows.

To clean or back up inside the private space, install KeepClear there too. Each copy sees only its own side.
If the phone keeps stopping the backup, allow it to run in the background. On this phone:
Similar photos

In "Choose what to delete", "Find similar photos" puts photos that look almost the same side by side, so you can compare them. You start it; it never runs by itself or in the background, and it works on this phone only, without the internet.

A photo marked "Suggested to keep" is larger or sharper than the others in its group, or has fewer areas that are too bright or too dark. It is only a suggestion: nothing is chosen, deleted or moved. When the photos are about equally good, KeepClear says there is no clear recommendation.

Photos from the camera and other memories can be backed up from there. Choosing photos to delete from a group comes in a later version.

With access to selected photos only, only those are compared. Some kinds of photos, like moving photos, can't be compared yet; the screen says how many.
